# DEAD AIR: voice-over script

<!-- generated by tools/voice_script.mjs from docs/voice/lines.json; edit the JSON, then run `npm run voice:script` -->

33 lines, 5 voices, in play order. The integration contract for the audio files is in [HANDOFF.md](HANDOFF.md); the
machine-readable version of this script is [lines.json](lines.json).

## How to read a line

```
ID · CHARACTER (channel)
engine: [sounds the game already plays under the line]          <- context only, never bake
> [bake tags] [delivery tags] The words, exactly as subtitled.   <- the TTS prompt (tts_text_full)
after: [sounds the game plays right after the line]
```

| bracket kind | examples | goes into the clip? |
|---|---|---|
| delivery (emotion, volume, breath) | `[shouting]` `[screaming in pain]` `[whispering]` `[long exhale]` `[voice breaking]` | yes, it is how the line is performed |
| bake tags (radio lines only) | `[radio squelch]` `[static]` | optional: bake them and set `radioBaked: true`, or leave them to the engine |
| engine sounds | `[siren]` `[shots]` `[gunfire]` `[rain]` `[heartbeat]` `[TV static]` | **no**, the game plays them, baking doubles them |

The words outside the brackets must stay exactly as written: the subtitle shows them, and the game
finds each clip by that text. `node tools/voice_script.mjs --check` fails if they drift.

## Cast

| id | character | subtitle | channel | voice |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dispatch` | DISPATCH | DISPATCH | radio | Keston City PD night dispatcher. Woman, mid-40s, American (Midwest), warm alto. Practised, flat radio cadence, clipped and efficient. The calm only cracks at the very end. |
| `officer` | OFC. R. HALLORAN #4471 | OFC. HALLORAN | body-mic | Patrol officer, man, late 30s, American, baritone. Dry, understated, tired from a night shift. Under pressure becomes breathless and raw; after the bite progressively weaker and slurred. He wears the camera, so he is the closest voice in every scene. |
| `swat` | SWAT ONE (team leader) | SWAT | distant-outdoor | Man, 40s, big chest voice, commanding. Shouting across 4 to 7 m of rainy courtyard. Also voices END-10 over his radio. |
| `swat2` | SWAT TWO | SWAT | distant-outdoor | Man, late 20s, higher tenor, tense, on the edge of panic. |
| `radio` | SWAT ONE (on radio) | RADIO | radio | Same actor as SWAT ONE, heard through a police radio. |

Channels: **radio** is heard through a police handheld or car radio (band-limited, squelch, a bed of static);
**body-mic** is Halloran himself, the camera is on his chest, so he is always the closest and driest voice;
**distant-outdoor** is shouted across 4 to 7 m of rainy courtyard, the game places it in 3-D at the speaker.

## Pronunciation

| written | say | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Twenty-one Adam fourteen / Adam fourteen / fourteen | as written | Halloran's call sign 21-A-14 (district 21, one-officer car "Adam", beat 14) |
| Keston | KESS-tun | the city; dispatch opens a call with it |
| code three | as written | respond with lights and siren |
| twenty-two fifty Wexley | as written | street number 2250 |
| unit one-C | as written | apartment 1C |
| zero three fourteen | as written | 03:14, 24-hour clock |
| Pell | rhymes with "bell" | Pell Street, where SWAT stages |
| SWAT one | "swot one" | the SWAT team leader's call sign |

## INT · Intro: the drive (evidence playback)

*Inside patrol car 21-A-14, 03:13 a.m., heavy rain, wipers, lights and siren (code 3). The bodycam's 30 s pre-event buffer ends with a double beep and audio cuts in. Radio traffic plays while the car waits at a red light, then turns into the Harlan Court lot.*

### INT-01 · DISPATCH (radio)

engine: [siren] [rain on the car roof] [wipers] [engine idling]

> [radio squelch] [static] [calm, clipped radio cadence] Twenty-one Adam fourteen, Keston. [urgent] Respond code three, twenty-two fifty Wexley Avenue, Harlan Court Apartments, unit one-C.

*First voice the player hears after the silent buffer. Routine but urgent.*

**When** intro, 0.8 s after the camera beep · **Blocking** yes, the scene waits for the line · **Length** game assumes 5.6 s · **Say** call sign 21-A-14 = "twenty-one Adam fourteen"; 2250 = "twenty-two fifty"; code three = lights and siren; "unit one-C" (apartment 1C)

### INT-02 · DISPATCH (radio)

engine: [siren] [rain on the car roof] [wipers]

> [radio squelch] [static] Multiple callers reporting screaming and an assault in progress. [slight hesitation] Caller advises the suspect is biting the victim.

*She reads it straight, but the last clause is strange even to her.*

**When** intro, after INT-01 · **Blocking** yes, the scene waits for the line · **Length** game assumes 5.9 s

### INT-03 · OFC. R. HALLORAN #4471 (body-mic)

engine: [siren] [rain on the car roof] [wipers]

> [tired, steady, raising his voice over the siren] Adam fourteen copies. I'm about a minute out.

*Keys the shoulder mic while glancing at the laptop. Night-shift weary.*

**When** intro, after INT-02 · **Blocking** yes, the scene waits for the line · **Length** game assumes 3.1 s

### INT-04 · DISPATCH (radio)

engine: [siren] [rain on the car roof] [wipers]

> [radio squelch] [static] Fourteen, be advised, [lower, heavier] we're holding six similar calls across the east district. [flat] Your backup is delayed.

*First hint that the night is wrong. Controlled, a touch slower.*

**When** intro, after INT-03 · **Blocking** yes, the scene waits for the line · **Length** game assumes 5.6 s

### INT-05 · OFC. R. HALLORAN #4471 (body-mic)

engine: [siren] [rain on the car roof]

> [long exhale] ...Copy.

after: [car pulls away]

*Resigned. One word after a breath.*

**When** intro, after INT-04; the red light turns green right after · **Blocking** yes, the scene waits for the line · **Length** game assumes 1.6 s, **clip max 2.0 s**

### INT-06 · OFC. R. HALLORAN #4471 (body-mic)

engine: [rain on the car roof] [engine idling]

> [quiet, keying the shoulder mic] Adam fourteen, on scene.

*Low, focused, looking at the dark building.*

**When** intro, car stopped in the lot · **Blocking** yes, the scene waits for the line · **Length** game assumes 1.7 s

### INT-07 · DISPATCH (radio)

engine: [rain on the car roof] [engine idling]

> [radio squelch] [static] [flat, procedural] Copy fourteen, on scene at zero three fourteen.

*Logging the time. Neutral.*

**When** intro, after INT-06 · **Blocking** yes, the scene waits for the line · **Length** game assumes 2.9 s · **Say** 03:14 = "zero three fourteen"

## LOB · Lobby

*Halloran enters the dark apartment-block lobby through a glass door. Fluorescent tubes buzz and flicker.*

### LOB-01 · OFC. R. HALLORAN #4471 (body-mic)

engine: [fluorescent tubes buzzing] [rain outside]

> [shouting into an empty lobby] Police department! [calling out] Anybody hurt in here? Call out!

*Projecting into a dark building, clearing it by the book.*

**When** player enters the lobby (trigger 'enterLobby', checkpoint 0) · **Blocking** no, it plays over gameplay · **Length** game assumes 3.1 s

## 1C · Apartment 1C: the bite

*A figure crouches over the building superintendent, feeding. Halloran confronts it at gunpoint; it lunges and bites his left forearm during a struggle. After the fight the victim gets back up.*

### 1C-01 · OFC. R. HALLORAN #4471 (body-mic)

engine: [wet feeding sounds] [TV static]

> [shouting, commanding, gun raised] Police! Get away from him!

*Full command voice, but it is his first sight of this.*

**When** entering 1C (trigger 'reach1C' or 'in1C'), camera push-in · **Blocking** yes, the scene waits for the line · **Length** game assumes 2.0 s

### 1C-02 · OFC. R. HALLORAN #4471 (body-mic)

engine: [TV static]

> [shouting, voice cracking with fear] Show me your hands! [louder] Now!

after: [the figure rises and lunges]

*The procedure is not working and he knows it.*

**When** 1C cutscene, after 1C-01 · **Blocking** yes, the scene waits for the line · **Length** game assumes 2.0 s

### 1C-03 · OFC. R. HALLORAN #4471 (body-mic)

engine: [bite] [struggle] [flesh tearing]

> [screaming in pain] Agh! It bit me! [panicked, struggling] Get off!

*Raw pain and panic, mid-struggle. Short.*

**When** 1.5 s into the grab, when the bite lands · **Blocking** no, it plays over gameplay · **Length** game assumes 2.4 s, **clip max 2.5 s**

### 1C-04 · OFC. R. HALLORAN #4471 (body-mic)

engine: [TV static]

> [breathing heavily, shaken, into the radio] Dispatch, Adam fourteen. Shots fired, suspect down. [pause] Victim is... [quiet] he's not breathing.

*Adrenaline crash. Trying to sound procedural and failing on the last words.*

**When** 1.6 s after the attacker dies · **Blocking** yes, the scene waits for the line · **Length** game assumes 4.5 s

### 1C-05 · DISPATCH (radio)

engine: [TV static]

> [radio squelch] [static] Fourteen, say again? [concerned] Are you injured?

*The first crack in her calm: concern for her officer.*

**When** 1C, while the victim twitches · **Blocking** yes, the scene waits for the line · **Length** game assumes 2.2 s

### 1C-06 · OFC. R. HALLORAN #4471 (body-mic)

engine: [TV static]

> [breathless, trying to hold it together] Dispatch... fourteen. [shaky] I've been bitten. The victim got back up. [voice breaking] They don't stop. [desperate] Send everything you've got.

*After killing the risen victim. The moment he understands.*

**When** 1.2 s after the risen victim dies · **Blocking** yes, the scene waits for the line · **Length** game assumes 6.2 s

### 1C-07 · DISPATCH (radio)


> [radio squelch] [static] [urgent, controlled] Copy fourteen. SWAT is staging on Pell Street. Can you get to the rear courtyard? They'll come in through the alley.

*Back to procedure, faster. She is holding it together for him.*

**When** after 1C-06 · **Blocking** yes, the scene waits for the line · **Length** game assumes 7.2 s · **Say** Pell Street, rhymes with "bell"

### 1C-08 · OFC. R. HALLORAN #4471 (body-mic)


> [heavy breathing] Rear courtyard. Copy.

*Short, determined.*

**When** after 1C-07 · **Blocking** yes, the scene waits for the line · **Length** game assumes 1.6 s

## CRT · Courtyard finale: hold until SWAT arrives

*Rear courtyard in the rain, waves of infected pouring in, continuous gunfire. Dispatch counts down on the radio (lines fire at 0, 40, 70 and 95 s).*

### CRT-01 · DISPATCH (radio)

engine: [rain] [gunfire] [infected screaming]

> [radio squelch] [static] [urgent, raising her voice over gunfire on the channel] Fourteen, SWAT is two minutes out. Hold the courtyard. They're coming through the alley.

*Clear and firm over chaos.*

**When** courtyard reached, finale timer 0 s · **Blocking** no, it plays over gameplay · **Length** game assumes 4.9 s

### CRT-02 · DISPATCH (radio)

engine: [rain] [gunfire] [infected screaming]

> [radio squelch] [static] [tense, encouraging] Sixty seconds, fourteen. Hang on.

*Personal for the first time: she is rooting for him.*

**When** finale timer 40 s · **Blocking** no, it plays over gameplay · **Length** game assumes 1.9 s

### CRT-03 · DISPATCH (radio)

engine: [rain] [gunfire] [infected screaming]

> [radio squelch] [static] [urgent] Thirty seconds. Units are on Pell.

**When** finale timer 70 s · **Blocking** no, it plays over gameplay · **Length** game assumes 2.2 s · **Say** Pell = street name, rhymes with "bell"

### CRT-04 · DISPATCH (radio)

engine: [rain] [gunfire] [infected screaming]

> [radio squelch] [static] [firm warning] SWAT is entering the alley. [emphatic] Do not fire toward the gate.

*A warning that matters. Slow down on the last clause.*

**When** finale timer 95 s · **Blocking** no, it plays over gameplay · **Length** game assumes 3.9 s

## END · Ending: the gate

*SWAT van in the alley, siren and red/blue lights. Two SWAT officers with rifle lights hold the gate. The infection takes Halloran mid-conversation; SWAT fires; the camera falls to the ground and records the aftermath.*

### END-01 · DISPATCH (radio)

engine: [siren in the alley] [rain]

> [radio squelch] [static] [careful, measured] Fourteen, SWAT has the rear gate. Walk to them, [slower] keep your hands where they can see them.

*She knows he has been bitten. Deliberately gentle.*

**When** after SWAT has shot the remaining infected in the courtyard · **Blocking** no, it plays over gameplay · **Length** game assumes 5.9 s

### END-02 · SWAT ONE (team leader) (distant-outdoor)

engine: [siren] [rain]

> [shouting from a distance, commanding] Keston SWAT! Drop the weapon! [louder] Drop it now!

*Rifle light in the officer's face. Standard challenge, maximum volume.*

**When** player within 7.5 m of the gate · **Blocking** yes, the scene waits for the line · **Length** game assumes 2.7 s

### END-03 · OFC. R. HALLORAN #4471 (body-mic)

engine: [siren] [rain]

> [shouting back, desperate] I'm a police officer! Twenty-one Adam fourteen!

*Lowering the gun. Pleading to be recognised.*

**When** after END-02 · **Blocking** yes, the scene waits for the line · **Length** game assumes 2.7 s · **Say** "twenty-one Adam fourteen"

### END-04 · SWAT TWO (distant-outdoor)

engine: [siren] [rain]

> [shouting, tense] Show me your arm. [sharper] Your left arm. [louder] Show me, now!

*He has seen the blood.*

**When** after END-03; the officer looks down at his bitten arm · **Blocking** yes, the scene waits for the line · **Length** game assumes 3.2 s

### END-05 · OFC. R. HALLORAN #4471 (body-mic)

engine: [heartbeat] [siren] [rain]

> [weak, slurred, unconvincing] It's... it's nothing. [forced] I'm fine.

*The infection is taking him. Lying, and failing.*

**When** after the arm reveal · **Blocking** yes, the scene waits for the line · **Length** game assumes 2.0 s

### END-06 · SWAT ONE (team leader) (distant-outdoor)

engine: [siren] [rain]

> [screaming, alarmed] He's bit! He's bit! [commanding] Get on the ground! On the ground!

after: [heartbeat] [infected moan] [radio glitch]

*Alarm spreading through the team.*

**When** after END-05 · **Blocking** yes, the scene waits for the line · **Length** game assumes 3.6 s

### END-07 · SWAT TWO (distant-outdoor)

engine: [siren] [rain]

> [screaming] Stop! STOP!

after: [shots] [shots] [shots] [camera hits the ground] [silence]

*The officer lurches forward. Pure reflex. Keep it short: the shots follow at once.*

**When** the turn: the camera lurches toward the gate · **Blocking** yes, the scene waits for the line · **Length** game assumes 1.6 s, **clip max 1.2 s**

### END-08 · SWAT ONE (team leader) (distant-outdoor)

engine: [rain] [siren]

> [breathing hard, procedural, shaken] Shots fired, shots fired. Suspect down.

*Training takes over. Recorded from the ground: he stands over the camera.*

**When** 1.2 s after the camera hits the ground · **Blocking** yes, the scene waits for the line · **Length** game assumes 2.1 s

### END-09 · SWAT TWO (distant-outdoor)

engine: [rain] [siren]

> [quiet, horrified] Wait... that's fourteen. [whispering] That's one of ours.

*Realisation. Barely audible on the last sentence.*

**When** after END-08 · **Blocking** yes, the scene waits for the line · **Length** game assumes 2.4 s

### END-10 · SWAT ONE (on radio) (radio)

engine: [rain] [siren]

> [radio squelch] [static] [flat, numb, procedural] Dispatch, SWAT one. We need a supervisor and a coroner at twenty-two fifty Wexley, rear alley.

*Holding his voice level by force.*

**When** after END-09 · **Blocking** yes, the scene waits for the line · **Length** game assumes 5.5 s · **Say** "twenty-two fifty Wexley"

### END-11 · DISPATCH (radio)

engine: [rain] [siren]

> [radio squelch] [static] [long pause] [voice breaking] ...Copy, SWAT one.

after: [signal lost]

*The last line of the game. She knew Halloran.*

**When** after END-10; the recording glitches out 1.2 s later · **Blocking** yes, the scene waits for the line · **Length** game assumes 1.6 s
